clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10142, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. Report deadline and status-quo period are not ends; functionally spent when the board reported and the statutory period ran, but the order remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10142 (15 FR 4465; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10142 and signed July 12, 1950. The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate the dispute between Braniff Airways, Inc. and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway & Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employees, requires the board to report within thirty days from the date of the order. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the board, its thirty-day report deadline and the status-quo sentence restating section 10 are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10142 with a subject line matching this order (creating an emergency board to investigate a airline labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The machine dossier did not locate the revoking provision for this pair; the held text of EO 12553 does contain the row for this order (number followed by a subject line) in the No. Subject table on its page 10, and the enacting sentence precedes the table, so the whole held EO 12553 text is cited as the ending source. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.
